Plan: Apple GPU support (issue #21)¶

Branch: 21-apple-gpu, from main at dea9c20 (after the CUDA work, PR #20, and the region export, PR #22). Status: steps 0–6 implemented (2026-10-20), PR #25; step 7 (macOS CI) dropped. The user tested the GUI on screen (2026-10-20). The numbers in §2 come from throwaway prototypes in the session scratch folder; they are not in the repository.

1. Goal¶

Issue #21: “extend support to the Apple GPU hardware set to allow GPU processing on non-CUDA devices.”

  • On a Mac, run the jobs that use the GPU on NVIDIA (#3) on the Apple GPU: the file waterfall, the live spectrum, and the channel filter of the dense demodulator and of the region export.

  • The same rules as for CUDA:

    • the GPU result looks the same as the CPU result;

    • any GPU error falls back to the CPU;

    • --gpu auto|on|off, the GPU checkbox and the status bar tag work the same way;

    • -DWVT_WITH_METAL=OFF builds what main builds now.

  • Other non-NVIDIA GPUs (AMD, Intel) are covered in §8, as a direction for later issues.

2. Findings on the development Mac¶

Apple M5, 10-core GPU, Metal 4, 16 GB of unified memory, macOS 26.6.2. Only the Command Line Tools are installed: no Xcode, so there is no offline Metal shader compiler (xcrun metal is missing). The SDK has Metal, Metal Performance Shaders (MPS), MPSGraph and Accelerate.

The test job is the inner loop of the waterfall and the live spectrum: complex samples, window, FFT, |X|², summed over frames.

Small jobs cost about 1 ms whatever their size. A new shape costs a graph compile of 11–97 ms the first time.

Metal compute kernel compiled at run time, reading the file in place¶

  • newLibraryWithSource compiles Metal Shading Language source at run time with only the Command Line Tools: 184 ms, once.

  • newBufferWithBytesNoCopy wraps a read-only mmap of the file: the GPU reads the file pages directly, with no copy.

  • A kernel that decodes ci16 and sums |x|² over 256 MB: 28.6 ms the first time (page faults), then 6.7–7.3 ms (36–40 GB/s). The sum matches the CPU.

  • maxBufferLength is 9.5 GB, and the recommended working set is 12.7 GB.

What this means¶

  1. vDSP alone makes every FFT on every Mac 2–6× faster, GPU or not, for little work.

  2. The GPU adds another 1.6–2.5× over vDSP on large jobs: the wide file waterfall and the channel filter. The live spectrum (2 MS per row at 61 MS/s) is about 1 ms either way.

  3. Unified memory removes the copies that the CUDA backend needs: no gather into pinned buffers, no upload. The GPU reads the mapped file.

  4. Apple GPUs have no 64-bit floating point. Two CUDA kernels use double:

    • the mixer phase (frac * index);

    • the cf64 decode.

    Both need another approach (§3).

3. Design decisions¶

Topic

Decision

Reason

API

Metal, in Objective-C++ (src/gpu/gpu_metal.mm), behind the existing backend interface (src/gpu/gpu_backend.h): gpuBackendProbe, gpuBackendSpectrogram, gpuBackendLive*, gpuBackendChannelize.

The rest of wvt does not change. Metal is the only supported GPU compute API on macOS (OpenCL is deprecated).

Kernels

Metal Shading Language source kept as a C++ string in gpu_metal.mm, compiled at run time when the backend first starts (about 0.2 s, on a background thread).

It builds without Xcode. A precompiled .metallib would need Xcode on every build machine.

FFT

MPSGraph fastFourierTransform (macOS 14 and later), between our own kernels. Cached graphs per (N, batch), with a power-of-two batch, as the cuFFT plan cache does.

Fast (§2), maintained by Apple, no extra dependency. The alternatives are below.

FFT alternatives

(a) Our own Stockham FFT kernel: no graph compile, full control, but more work and tuning. (b) VkFFT with its Metal backend: one more third-party library, but it is also a route to Vulkan, HIP and OpenCL (§8).

Can replace MPSGraph later behind the same code, if the graph compile time matters.

File input

newBufferWithBytesNoCopy over the page-aligned mapping, one buffer per chunk (offset rounded down to a page, at most 1 GB), so files larger than maxBufferLength work. IqFile exposes the mapping.

No gather and no copy (§2).

Mixer phase

A 64-bit fixed-point phase: the host computes the increment inc = round(frac · 2⁶⁴) and the chunk’s start phase in0 · inc (unsigned 64-bit, wrapping). The kernel adds k · inc (ulong) and takes the top 32 bits as the phase in cycles.

Metal has ulong but no double. The phase stays exact for any file length; the error is far below the float rounding of the samples. The CUDA and CPU mixers can use the same method later.

cf64 files

Decoded on the CPU to cf32 for that chunk (or the GPU path reports Unavailable for cf64 at first).

No double in Metal. cf64 is rare.

CPU FFT

On macOS, FFT::forward (src/dsp/dsp.cpp) uses vDSP (vDSP_fft_zip, with a split-complex buffer per thread). Other systems keep the radix-2 code.

2–6× for every FFT on every Mac (§2), with or without the GPU. Separate commit, separate test.

Build

WVT_WITH_METAL = AUTO / ON / OFF, default AUTO, on Apple only. CMake enables OBJCXX and links Metal, Foundation, MetalPerformanceShaders and MetalPerformanceShadersGraph. CUDA stays Linux-only, so a build has at most one GPU backend.

Same pattern as WVT_WITH_CUDA. No new dependency to install.

Run time

gpuInit finds the default Metal device. It needs macOS 14 or later (MPSGraph complex FFT); on older macOS the reason is logged and the CPU is used. Intel Macs with AMD or Intel graphics also have Metal; they are not tested.

The same --gpu rules and log lines as CUDA.

Names

Messages that say “CUDA” become neutral: “built without GPU support”, GpuInfo::backend = “CUDA” or “Metal”, gpu_check prints the backend. The status bar shows GPU Apple M5.

Two backends now.

Budgets

The GPU budgets (2 G samples for the waterfall, 100 MS/s live) apply to Metal too. Set them again from gpu_check --bench on this Mac.

The same knobs.

Concurrency

One MTLDevice and its compiled pipelines, shared. Each user thread has its own command queue, buffers and graph cache (thread_local), as with CUDA streams.

Same structure as the CUDA backend.

Live spectrum

Uses the GPU only when frames × N is large enough to pay for the about 1 ms per call (measure; else the vDSP CPU path).

§2: small jobs are not faster on the GPU.

4. Interface changes¶

  • src/gpu/gpu_backend.h: no new functions. GpuInfo gets backend (“CUDA” / “Metal”).

  • src/io/iq_file.h: mappedBase() and mappedSize(). The mapping is already page-aligned (mmap). data() (the raw bytes) stays.

  • src/dsp/dsp.cpp: FFT holds a vDSP setup on Apple. forward() keeps its interface (in-place, interleaved cf), and converts to split complex inside.

5. Implementation steps¶

Each step builds and passes the tests, then gets its own commit.

  1. Benchmark first. gpu_check --bench on this Mac, before any change. These are the CPU numbers to beat.

  2. vDSP CPU FFT (src/dsp/dsp.cpp, Apple only).

    • All self-tests must pass.

    • gpu_check compares the vDSP FFT with the radix-2 one (strong bins within 0.05 dB) and times it.

    • The waterfall checksums change (a different FFT); the 0.05 dB rule is the test now.

  3. Build switch and Metal probe.

    • WVT_WITH_METAL in CMake, and src/gpu/gpu_metal.mm with gpuBackendProbe and gpuBackendList.

    • Neutral names (§3), GpuInfo::backend.

    • --list-devices shows the Metal device.

    • --gpu on works, and the status bar shows the tag.

  4. Kernels and the waterfall.

    • The MSL source: decode with window, accumulate, pool.

    • Zero-copy chunks of the mapping.

    • MPSGraph FFT in the same command buffer.

    • gpu_check runs its GPU vs CPU comparisons, which can run on this Mac.

  5. Live spectrum. GpuLiveSpectrum on Metal (the ring slice as a shared buffer), with the size threshold of §3.

  6. Channel filter.

    • Mix with the fixed-point phase (§3), and the direct FIR with the taps in threadgroup memory.

    • gpu_check and extract_check compare with the CPU.

    • The region export (#18) uses it with no change.

  7. Budgets and README.

    • Set the budgets from gpu_check --bench.

    • README: “Optional: GPU acceleration” covers Metal; the file table.

  8. CI.

    • A macos-14 (Apple Silicon) job: install XQuartz (brew install --cask xquartz), build, run the self-tests.

    • GitHub’s Mac runners are virtual machines. If they have no Metal device, the GPU checks are skipped, as on Linux.

6. Testing¶

Where

What

This Mac (M5)

Everything: the build with no warnings, all self-tests, gpu_check comparisons on the real GPU (waterfall and live within 0.05 dB, channel filter within 1e-4), gpu_check --bench, WVT_GPU_FORCE_FAIL=1, the GUI (tag, checkbox, (GPU) in live mode, an export with a band).

-DWVT_WITH_METAL=OFF

The same as main, apart from the vDSP FFT (step 1).

Linux CI

No change: the CPU and CUDA jobs still pass.

macOS CI (step 7)

The build and the self-tests on Apple Silicon.

7. Acceptance criteria¶

  1. On this Mac, gpu_check passes on the Metal GPU.

  2. The file waterfall at N 8192 over 100× the zoom-1 span: at least 3× faster than the CPU (vDSP) path, and “FFT sees 100 %” for views at least 4× wider than the CPU budget allows.

  3. The channel filter with 8191 taps: at least 5× faster than the CPU.

  4. A forced GPU error falls back to the CPU and logs a WARN.

  5. -DWVT_WITH_METAL=OFF and Linux builds behave as before.

8. Other non-NVIDIA GPUs (AMD, Intel): options for later¶

The backend interface in gpu_backend.h keeps this open. Options, from the least work for one vendor to the widest reach:

Route

GPUs

FFT

Notes

HIP (ROCm)

AMD on Linux

hipFFT / rocFFT

hipify turns gpu_cuda.cu into HIP almost line for line. ROCm supports a limited list of AMD cards (mostly RDNA2/3 and Instinct). The cheapest route for AMD.

SYCL / oneAPI

Intel (also AMD, NVIDIA through plugins)

oneMKL DFT

A large toolchain. Mainly useful for Intel Arc and data-center GPUs.

Vulkan compute

AMD, Intel, NVIDIA on Linux and Windows; Apple through MoltenVK

VkFFT (MIT, header-only)

One backend for all vendors. More code than CUDA (descriptors, SPIR-V shaders at build or run time). VkFFT also has CUDA, HIP, OpenCL, Level Zero and Metal backends.

OpenCL

Most GPUs

VkFFT (OpenCL backend) or clFFT

Wide reach, but old: deprecated on macOS, and uneven drivers on Linux.

Recommendation: do the Metal backend for #21 now. For AMD and Intel, open a new issue when there is a computer to test on. HIP is the shortest route for AMD on Linux, and Vulkan + VkFFT is the route to cover every vendor with one backend.

9. Decisions needed¶

  1. Scope: Metal backend plus the vDSP CPU FFT (recommended), or Metal only? vDSP helps every Mac and is low risk.

  2. FFT on the GPU: MPSGraph (recommended: fast, no dependency, needs macOS 14 or later), our own Metal FFT kernel (no graph compile, more work), or VkFFT’s Metal backend (one more library, a route to other vendors)?

  3. Minimum macOS for the GPU path: 14 (Sonoma), as MPSGraph’s complex FFT needs? Older macOS uses the CPU.

  4. cf64 on the GPU: decode on the CPU for that chunk, or no GPU for cf64 files at first?

  5. macOS CI job (step 7): add it? On a private repository, macOS minutes cost 10× Linux minutes.

  6. AMD / Intel: a separate issue later (recommended), or part of #21?

10. Decisions (2026-10-20)¶

  1. Scope: the Metal backend and the vDSP CPU FFT.

  2. GPU FFT: MPSGraph.

  3. Minimum macOS for the GPU path: 14. Older macOS uses the CPU.

  4. cf64: decoded on the CPU, chunk by chunk.

  5. macOS CI job: skipped (step 7 is dropped).

  6. AMD / Intel: a separate issue, #24.

11. Implementation notes¶

Change of plan: a hybrid FFT¶

With MPSGraph for every FFT, the GPU waterfall was only 1.0–1.4× the CPU per sample on the M5. The CPU had just become 2–2.4× faster with vDSP (step 1), and the MPSGraph pipeline moves each sample through memory four times: decode, FFT in, FFT out, sum. A prototype kernel that decodes, windows, transforms and squares one FFT in threadgroup memory ran at 4.1–4.5 GS/s (2.5–3× the CPU), but only up to N 4096 (32 KB of threadgroup memory). The user chose the hybrid (2026-10-20):

  • N ≤ 4096: our one-pass kernel fftPower (radix-2 in threadgroup memory; the fftshifted powers of each FFT go out), then accumulatePower sums them per row.

  • N 8192–65536: decodeWindow, the MPSGraph FFT and accumulate, in one command buffer.

Change

FFT uses vDSP on macOS (a split-complex scratch per thread).

src/gpu/gpu_metal.mm

The Metal backend: device probe and list, the kernels (MSL source compiled at run time, safe math mode), no-copy buffers over the file mapping (up to 1 GB per chunk), the waterfall (hybrid), the live spectrum, the channel filter (64-bit fixed-point phase, taps in threadgroup memory up to 8192). cf64 is decoded on the CPU.

src/gpu/gpu.h, src/gpu/gpu_backend.h, src/gpu/gpu_common.cpp

GpuInfo::backend; gpuBackendName, gpuBackendImplements (the jobs a backend runs), GpuLimits / gpuBackendLimits (budgets and the job sizes below which the CPU is faster).

The new backend functions; CUDA keeps its limits. Neutral “built without GPU support”.

The FFT against a direct DFT; the backend name; why a comparison is skipped; the bench shows the GPU budget and minimum.

Results on the M5 (gpu_check, gpu_check --bench)¶

  • Correctness, GPU against CPU:

    • waterfall: every format, big-endian, swapped I/Q, header, edges and long rows, within 0.0002 dB;

    • live: within 0.0002 dB;

    • channel filter: within 1.1e-6 of the peak (the limit is 1e-4).

    Cancel and the forced failure work on all three paths.

  • vDSP CPU FFT: waterfall 2.0–2.4× faster than before, live row 2.3×.

  • GPU waterfall:

    • N 1024 at 100× zoom: 39 ms against 61 ms on the CPU (1.6×), the same FFTs.

    • N 8192 and 65536 (MPSGraph): 1.2–1.4× per sample. Wide views get more coverage for about the same time.

  • Live row, N 2048: 0.72 / 1.76 / 2.86 ms on the GPU against 2.43 / 4.88 / 7.26 ms on one CPU core, at 20 / 40 / 61.44 MS/s.

  • Channel filter (8 MS in, decimation 8, with the demodulation on the CPU): 1.8× (255 taps), 3.7× (2047), 6.2× (8191).

  • Acceptance (§7):

    • item 1 (gpu_check on the GPU), item 4 (fallback) and item 5 (OFF and Linux builds): met;

    • item 3 (≥ 5× for 8191 taps): met;

    • item 2 (≥ 3× at N 8192): not met. N 8192 uses MPSGraph, about 1.2×. A multi-pass FFT of our own (the third option of decision 2) would be needed for that.

Checks¶

  • The macOS build has no warnings; all 6 self-tests pass.

  • -DWVT_WITH_METAL=OFF: builds the stub (“built without GPU support”).

  • The CUDA 12.8 container build still compiles with no warnings, and its self-tests pass.

GUI¶

The user tested the GUI on screen (2026-10-20). All five checks passed:

  • the status bar showed GPU Apple M5;

  • the GPU checkbox switched the GPU off and on;

  • live mode showed (GPU);

  • a region export with a band worked;

  • WVT_GPU_FORCE_FAIL=1 gave the CPU tag with the reason in the tooltip.
